title: The winning crab
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The morning after the derby. The winning crab, weighed, drawn, let go — the uncle's rule. Gully holds it up for Wood to draw it first. Wood draws it fast. It goes back in the bay. The strip has the only copy.

panels.composition: The dock, morning. GULLY holding up an enormous Dungeness by the back. WOOD with the pad, fast. BARNABY beside himself.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager holding up a huge crab by its back on a dock while a young man draws fast and a small dog leaps, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the crab, in the flyer's line, but alive — the legs the right number, the strip counted.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a fast ink drawing of a large live crab, legs exact, black and white, no words
a stocky teenager on a dock holding a crab, plain, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The crab going back into the bay from Gully's hands. The splash. The dog at the edge. The drawing the only copy. That's the trophy.

image.prompt: a large crab being released from a teenager's hands into gray bay water from a dock, a small dog at the edge, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Weigh it, draw it, let it go. The uncle's rule. The strip keeps the only copy.
